To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
coronary flow reserve increases in fetal sheep after chronic adenosine infusion.
chronic intracorony infusion of adenosin in the near term fetal sheep increases coronary blood flow, coronary flow reserve, and coronary conductance.
chronic coronary vasodilation in the near-term ovine fetus results in an increase in coronary vascular growth, which is associated with an increase in coronary conductance and coronary flow reserve.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of the coronary vascular system in the fetus.
the development of the fetal coronary circulation, and the mechanisms by which it responds to stress and hypoxemia.
the regulation of coronary blood flow in the ovine fetus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

chronic coronary vasodilation in the near-term fetal myocardium increases coronary blood flow and coronary vascular growth, which may be important for the development of the fetal coronary circulation.
the coronary vascular bed is capable of adapting to chronic changes in coronary blood flow in the near-term fetus, and this adaptation is not dependent on hypoxia.
the increase in coronary blood flow in the fetal sheep heart is associated with an increase in coronary vascular growth, which is independent of tissue hypoxemia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
adenosine is a potent coronary vasodilator in the fetal lamb, but it also stimulates coronary growth.
the coronary vasculature of the fetal sheep heart is capable of growth in response to chronic increases in coronary blood flow without hypoxia.
chronic increases in coronary flow in fetal sheep without changes in hemodynamic stress or hypoxia increase the number and size of the coronary resistance vessels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the heart has the capacity to adapt to increased coronary flow demands by increasing the size of the coronary resistance vessels.
the fetal coronary circulation is capable of responding to increased blood flow with increased growth of coronary resistance arterioles.
coronary flow is a major determinant of the growth of coronary resistance vasculature.
